correctness.rationale: PASS: Complete graph K_n centered nonnegative ball maximal is exactly M f_i=max(f_i, arithmetic mean f). On each strict mean-comparison chamber S, branch A_S is constant-preserving and copies h_i for i in S, mean h otherwise. Coarea gives exact complete-pair Gini norm from binary cuts. Independently derived exact branch-cut identity R=x(n-x)/(n*l)+z(n-z)/(n*(n-l)), with l=|U|, x=|S∩U|, z=|S\U|. Maximizing x<=l<=n/2 gives x(n-x)<=l(n-l), maximizing z gives floor(n²/4), and the convex endpoint m+floor(n²/4)/m on m∈[ceil(n/2),n-1] yields n>=3 coefficient 1+floor((n-2)²/4)/(n(n-1)). n=2 explicit half difference separately. Reconstructed exact integer cardinality constraints and cut ratios exhaustively for n=2,...,24 (including n=24 value 673/552); exact attaining input 1_S with one vertex raised within same strict chamber. No signed absolute-value conclusion is claimed; constant-shift counterexamples show that variant fails. No numerical extrapolation to all n.

value.rationale: PASS: Sharp nonlinear stability of the canonical complete-graph maximal averaging operator in all dimensions, with exact finite-n transition from nonexpansive to expansive pairwise variation and asymptotic ceiling 5/4. The difference from strong individual-signal smoothing directly informs sensitivity of finite-graph filtering and makes a natural complete classification.

limitations: A hidden theorem for sharp two-input complete-graph maximal operator under mean-clipping language could cover this exact factor.
The signed-input |f| maximal operator loses translation-equivariance, so the result must be kept to nonnegative signals.
The original n=2 special case differs discontinuously from n>=3 formula; it was separately verified.
The frozen repository tree and original public metadata were read; source public AUDIT.json and METADATA.json include operational scope_run_id, so no public import is authorized from this review.
